historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue and EPS CAGRs (both computed on the SEC-XBRL-corrected series, see inputs.notes) diverge sharply from equity CAGR and from each other -- revenue fell -7.5% p.a. over 3yr and EPS fell -30.7% p.a. over 3yr purely because FY2022 was a crush-margin/commodity-price peak (EPS $7.71) and FY2025 a trough (EPS $2.23), with owner-FCF also swinging from -9.9% margin (FY2019) to +6.2% (FY2021). None of these historical CAGRs are used as the forward growth driver -- a flat ~2% volume-growth assumption is used instead, per inputs.notes, because this is a mature scale commodity processor whose revenue is overwhelmingly a function of ag commodity prices, not a compounding growth trajectory. Equity CAGR (2.6%) is the most representative growth proxy of the three and is used only as the historical-growth disclosure, not literally as the projected revenue growth rate.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 guidance is a genuine but partly cyclical/policy-driven upswing (crush margins, 45Z, Nutrition recovery); the model gives it partial credit in year 1 then reverts to a ~5.0% through-cycle EBITDA margin, never capitalizing either the FY2022 peak or the FY2024-25 trough in perpetuity.
scenario_narratives.bull: RVO/45Z tailwinds prove durable, low-capital-intensity crush debottlenecking delivers high returns, and Nutrition's post-scandal recovery compounds -- margin holds near the FY2022 cycle peak.
scenario_narratives.bear: Biofuel policy reverses (RVOs/45Z rolled back or challenged), crush margins stay at the FY2024-25 trough, Nutrition's recovery stalls again amid ongoing SEC/shareholder litigation, and leverage becomes a real constraint.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ADM is a highly cyclical, thin-margin global agribusiness processor whose reported earnings swing 3-4x through the crush-margin and biofuel-policy cycle (FY2022 EPS $7.71 at the peak vs FY2025 EPS $2.23 at the trough, further depressed by the 2024 Nutrition segment accounting scandal). The FY2026 guidance raise reflects a real earnings recovery -- record 2026-2027 EPA Renewable Volume Obligations, a raised ~$250M 45Z tax-credit benefit, and genuine Nutrition segment improvement -- but a large share of it is policy-contingent and management itself flags limited forward visibility (~30% of Q4 2026 crush volume locked). This DCF is built on a mid-cycle-normalized owner-FCF basis: year-1 margins give partial credit to the current upswing, then mean-revert over 3-4 years to a ~5.0% through-cycle EBITDA margin (between the FY2022 peak of 6.5% and the FY2025 trough of 3.8%) rather than extrapolating either the FY2026 guidance spike or the FY2024-25 trough into perpetuity. A low terminal cap multiple (10x, house default 20x) reflects ADM's own trading history and a business with essentially no pricing power. Note: FY2022-2025 revenue in the source data was corrected before this build -- the SEC XBRL ingestion had captured a ~3-4x-too-small revenue subset tag (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax) instead of the actual GAAP total (Revenues); the corrected series now shows sane 6-8% gross margins consistent with a commodity processor.
key_risks_to_valuation: Biofuel policy reversal (RVO rollback, 45Z credit repeal or legal challenge) would remove a growing and currently un-hedged share of FY2026-27 profit
Only ~30% of Q4 2026 North American crush volume was locked as of the Q2 2026 call -- forward earnings visibility is genuinely limited even after the guidance raise
Nutrition segment credibility is still rebuilding post-scandal; the litigated SEC action against the former CFO and ongoing shareholder class actions are live tail risk
Net debt of ~$6.5B against a thin, cyclical EBITDA base (net debt/EBITDA ~2.1-2.7x through-cycle) means a sustained margin downturn pressures coverage and could raise the effective cost of capital
Global crop supply/demand and weather risk (South American harvest, China purchasing behavior) directly moves origination volumes and crush spreads independent of company execution

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap StockBasedCompensation (cash flow add-back), FY2025 10-K; ADM does not separately disclose cash tax withheld on net-share settlement, so this is the cash-flow add-back only
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.7% built on USD flows: ~4.2% 10yr UST (Sep-2026) + ~4.5pp ERP/size premium appropriate for a highly cyclical, capital-intensive, thin-margin commodity processor with BBB-ish leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~2.1-2.7x through cycle)
inputs.lease_treatment: ADM's operating leases are not material to the flows (no separate lease-principal or lease-liability disclosure surfaced in XBRL extraction); treated as embedded in EBITDA/capex, consistent with US GAAP lessee expensing for most of ADM's lease book -- no separate adjustment applied
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial -- ADM does not carry a disclosed material NCI stake; net income used as reported (attributable to ADM common stockholders)
inputs.notes: Route: owner-FCF component DCF via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md (operating company, cyclical industrial processor) + owner-fcf-adaptations.md section 7f (charge cyclicality risk once, in the flows, via mid-cycle margin normalization -- not stacked again as a WACC premium). MID-CYCLE NORMALIZATION APPLIED: ADM is a classic crush-margin/biofuel-policy cyclical. FY2022 was a margin peak (EBITDA margin 6.5%, EPS $7.71) driven by the 2021-22 commodity price spike; FY2024-2025 was a trough (EBITDA margin 3.8-4.8%, EPS $3.65/$2.23) compounded by the Nutrition segment accounting scandal, SEC investigation costs and a weak crush environment. FY2026 guidance ($5.15-5.60 adjusted EPS, up sharply from $4.15-4.70) reflects a real but partly policy-driven upswing: record 2026-2027 EPA Renewable Volume Obligations and a raised ~$250M 45Z tax-credit benefit. Management itself flags only ~30% of Q4 2026 crush volume was locked as of the Q2 call -- i.e. even management does not treat the current run-rate as fully secured. The base case therefore anchors year-1 EBITDA margin to the FY2026 guided level (partial credit to the upswing, since RVOs are now locked in through 2027 and Nutrition's recovery looks structural) then MEAN-REVERTS over years 2-4 toward a ~5.0-5.3% through-cycle average (between the 3.8% trough and 6.5% peak, closer to the FY2021-2023 average of ~5.3-6.5%) before drifting to a 5.0% terminal margin -- never capitalizing the peak or the trough in perpetuity. Revenue held roughly flat-to-low-single-digit growth (a scale commodity processor, not a growth business; the 2020-2025 revenue swings from $64B to $102B back to $80B are overwhelmingly commodity price/FX, not volume growth) using a 2.0% base path (roughly global grain/oilseed demand growth) rather than any historical CAGR, since the raw revenue CAGRs here are dominated by commodity-price cycles and a genuine tag-selection data fix (see below), not organic growth. Terminal cap multiple set at 10x (cyclical commodity processor -- lower than the house 20x default and even the 12-15x 'cyclical' floor, reflecting ADM's own trading history rarely above ~12-14x EV/EBITDA and a business with essentially no pricing power). Cash tax rate ramped to a 23% through-cycle statutory-equivalent rate (recent effective rates of 5.4%-20.9% are noisy and include one-off credits/valuation items; 23% is close to the FY2023 rate, ADM's cleanest recent year). DATA CORRECTION: core_metrics.revenue for FY2022-FY2025 (and Q1 2024 onward quarterly) was wrong on ingestion -- build_facts_xbrl.py had picked up us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax (a ~3-4x smaller subset ADM began disclosing alongside its GAAP total) instead of us-gaap:Revenues (the actual income-statement total, continuously reported every year, e.g. FY2025 $80,269M not the $24,956M previously stored). Corrected via 15 `make fix` calls before this build (see research/ADM/Reports/ADM_Corrections.jsonl) -- gross margins now read a sane 6-8% instead of a nonsensical 20-30%, consistent with a commodity processor. This DCF is built on the corrected series.

bear.narrative: The 45Z credit and 2026-2027 RVOs are rolled back or legally challenged, crush margins revert to the FY2024-2025 trough and stay there (management's own disclosure that only ~30% of Q4 2026 volume was locked is the tell), Nutrition's recovery stalls again (a repeat of the pre-scandal underperformance or a fresh disclosure issue given the still-litigated former-CFO SEC action and ongoing shareholder suits), and a China trade disruption or a weak South American harvest further pressures origination volumes. EBITDA margin sits near the FY2025 trough (3.8-4.5%) for the full horizon; leverage (net debt/EBITDA already ~2.1-2.7x) becomes a real constraint if margins stay depressed, raising the discount rate.

base.narrative: FY2026 guidance ($5.15-5.60 adjusted EPS) reflects a real crush-margin and 45Z tax-credit upswing (record 2026-2027 EPA RVOs, raised ~$250M 45Z benefit) layered on a genuine Nutrition segment recovery (Q2 2026 operating profit +51% YoY, Decatur East ramp, Asia-Pacific flavor strength). The base case gives partial credit to this upswing in year 1 (EBITDA margin 5.7%, between the FY2025 trough of 3.8% and the FY2026 run-rate implied by guidance) then mean-reverts over 4 years to a 5.0% through-cycle margin -- roughly the FY2021-2023 average -- reflecting management's own caution that only ~30% of Q4 2026 crush volume was locked as of the Q2 call, and that biofuel-policy tailwinds (RVOs, 45Z) are political and can moderate. Revenue held to a flat 2% volume-growth path since ADM's top line is overwhelmingly a function of ag-commodity prices, not organic volume growth. Cash tax rate ramps to 23%, close to ADM's cleanest recent year (FY2023, 19.2% effective) and modestly below the US statutory-plus-state blended rate, reflecting continued 45Z/biofuel credits. Working capital modelled with a negative capture (-8%) on revenue growth, appropriate for a commodity merchant/processor whose receivables and inventory scale with -- and slightly exceed -- revenue growth (the opposite sign from a prepaid-subscription business).

bull.narrative: The 2026-2027 RVO/45Z policy tailwind proves durable rather than transitory (no adverse EPA rulemaking or legal challenge), crush debottlenecking projects deliver the high returns management expects at roughly a quarter of greenfield capital intensity, and the Nutrition segment's post-scandal recovery compounds -- natural colors ($80-100M opportunity), Asia-Pacific flavor growth and Decatur East all scale as guided. Margin holds near the FY2022 cycle-peak level (5.8-6.5%) rather than fully reverting, and China continues buying North American soybeans without a renewed trade disruption.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 15% house default to 30% because ADM's current earnings upswing is unusually policy-dependent (a growing share of FY2026 profit rests on RVOs and the 45Z credit, both politically reversible) and because management's own disclosure that only ~30% of Q4 2026 crush volume was locked as of the Q2 call signals real near-term earnings-visibility risk even after the guidance raise. Litigation overhang (litigated SEC action against the former CFO, ongoing shareholder class actions over the Nutrition accounting scandal) is a second, correlated risk to the same downside case. Bull weight trimmed to 25% because it requires several independent things to hold simultaneously (durable biofuel policy, sustained crush strength, AND a full Nutrition turnaround) rather than any one of them.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
